## Purpose

Apply an explicit request from Jack to close an issue after he rejects its
investigation report. Rejection alone leaves the issue open. See the
[triage guide](../../guides/github-issue-triage.md).

## When a playbook uses it

The `close-explicit-rejection` rule calls it for a `reject` `review.decided`
event. The review service separately creates a response task for revisions.

## How it works internally

`GitHubIssueCommandsMixin._cmd_github_issue_rejection` in
`src/commands/github_issue_commands.py` verifies the current review revision
and reads Jack's decision note and comments. It closes the issue only when
they explicitly request closure and do not ask to keep it open.

## Side effects and persistence

When closure is authorized, the GitHub client posts Jack's reason and closes
the issue. The closing comment has a stable marker so a retry does not post it
twice. Other rejection feedback does not write to GitHub.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

An unrelated or stale event, or rejection without an explicit close request,
returns `ignored`. Invalid project input or GitHub access failure returns
`rejected`. Inspect failures with `aq playbook show-run <run-id>`.

## Example step

The `close-explicit-rejection` rule passes the event's `project_id`,
`review_id`, and `revision` to `github_issue_rejection`. `closed` and
`ignored` complete the rule.
